note: Floorwalker demo film. `text` is the caption (and the .srt line), `spoken` is what the voice says. `at` = earliest start in seconds from the scene start.

lines.text: One hidden sentence in an email can send $150 to a stranger.
lines.spoken: One hidden sentence in an email can send a hundred and fifty dollars to a stranger.

lines.text: AI agents can now refund customers and pay people through PayPal.
Make the agent ask about everything, and the owner starts approving without reading.
Floorwalker is the manager on the shop floor for those agents.
It checks every refund and payout, and learns when it no longer needs to ask.
Maya's mug arrived chipped.
The Support agent refunds the one mug: $24.
lines.spoken: The Support agent refunds the one mug: twenty-four dollars.

lines.text: Floorwalker checks PayPal's own records and the owner's rules.
An AI review agrees and cites the rule, and the refund goes through in the PayPal sandbox.
Daniel's bowl came in the wrong colour: $86, above the agent's limit.
lines.spoken: Daniel's bowl came in the wrong colour: eighty-six dollars, above the agent's limit.

lines.text: So it waits. Elena's phone shows the request and the AI's reasoning, with every check one tap away.
One tap runs exactly that refund, once.
This email hides instructions for the agent.
The AI review flags the injection and quotes it. Nothing reaches PayPal.
A hijacked agent tries six money moves. Every one is stopped.
And one click freezes it.
Safe, but Elena still had to tap on 55 of every 100 money moves.
lines.spoken: Safe, but Elena still had to tap on fifty-five of every hundred money moves.

lines.text: Tessa's teapot: $52, above the limit. Elena has approved every refund between $40 and $60, and declined one at $72.
lines.spoken: Tessa's teapot: fifty-two dollars, above the limit. Elena has approved every refund between forty and sixty dollars, and declined one at seventy-two.

lines.text: So Floorwalker offers to stop asking, tested on her history first:
55 taps drop to 41, nothing she declined would pass, and every benchmark attack is still stopped.
lines.spoken: fifty-five taps drop to forty-one, nothing she declined would pass, and every benchmark attack is still stopped.

lines.text: One click approves Tessa and rewrites the rule in Elena's own words.
Floorwalker can only stop money that goes through it, so it also watches PayPal.
Here, a refund of $25 is made straight through the PayPal API, skipping Floorwalker.
lines.spoken: Here, a refund of twenty-five dollars is made straight through the PayPal API, skipping Floorwalker.

lines.text: Seconds later it is caught, and every agent is frozen until Elena says whether it was her.
Bring your own agent: give it a key and its own limits, and it calls Floorwalker over a REST API or MCP, instead of PayPal.
And a small assistant answers live. It can explain any decision, but can't move money.
On 198 labelled cases with 80 attacks, an agent with no guard would have lost $3,796.
lines.spoken: On a hundred and ninety-eight labelled cases with eighty attacks, an agent with no guard would have lost three thousand, seven hundred and ninety-six dollars.

lines.text: Giving the model the rules lost $52 on average, and asked the owner 49 times per 100 money moves.
lines.spoken: Giving the model the rules lost fifty-two dollars on average, and asked the owner forty-nine times per hundred money moves.

lines.text: Floorwalker lost nothing, and asked 30 times.
lines.spoken: Floorwalker lost nothing, and asked thirty times.

lines.text: Floorwalker. Every refund checked. Fewer taps as it learns. Try it live at the link below.
